objective: GroupGuard only handles command intake, intranet requests, protocol validation, and OneBot delivery. Public upstream access, business processing, rendering, caching, and degradation are owned by lolapisevers.

failed_attempt_fixed.cause: The shard release gate reused the ARAM forward fixture without changing feature=aram, and the production request helper correctly rejected it as delivery_feature_mismatch.
failed_attempt_fixed.fix: Use a cloned forward fixture with feature=shard while preserving the same validated forward delivery shape.

steps.summary: Pinned the service fixtures, added strict delivery parsing and image integrity checks, converted validated payloads to OneBot plans, and proved the new client makes one intranet request with no public fallback.

steps.implementation_scope: shard command and shard admin tester
steps.summary: The real shard command and admin tester share the strict delivery request path and passed the complete GroupGuard test and SnowLuma build gates. Production rollout remains blocked until the compatible lolapisevers release exposes the contract on port 5001.

A priority-90 native command plugin owns 查合集, sends the original hero text to the intranet delivery endpoint, validates the response, and sends final text, Base64 image, or forward nodes. The legacy interaction trigger no longer claims 查合集, so plugin-side public downloads and local hero matching are not reachable from the command dispatcher.
Move ARAM and ban commands to the final delivery envelope; battle-query migration is handled only after its delivery feature is defined.
The shard overview and tester use LOL API Base; public shard and hero URL fields remain visible only as deprecated legacy configuration until the wider LoL migration is complete.

The green release gate proves one intranet request, no public fallback, raw nickname forwarding, strict image conversion, forward conversion, legacy trigger removal, fixed transport failure handling, SnowLuma build success, and cross-repository mock compatibility. Repository-wide removal of all legacy LoL public providers remains part of GG-LOL-UNIFY-001.
The GroupGuard shard code is green but must not be deployed until production lolapisevers /build-info confirms the compatible release containing /api/v1/groupguard/query.

current_findings.summary: Repository evidence still reports production on bd2d92996f8c7af4e6fd51f021f1546bda250a8a while the compatible release target is 8de85a855b8338c3a9a69cbb2a937cd0a6ef8b82. GroupGuard production deployment is blocked until /build-info and the delivery endpoint confirm the target release.

The old public shard loader and local formatter remain as unreachable migration code after the legacy 查合集 trigger was removed. Delete them only after production acceptance; they must never be re-registered as a fallback.
The built-in ban path still supports direct public providers when the intranet base is absent; this remains blocked work for GG-LOL-UNIFY-001.
Battle, ARAM and ban legacy handlers still interpret or format business data. This shard PR intentionally does not broaden into those commands before the service release gate is satisfied.

next_recommended_action.summary: Run the prepared v6 safe service deployment, obtain completed deployment and verification records, confirm /build-info reports 8de85a855b8338c3a9a69cbb2a937cd0a6ef8b82, and verify POST /api/v1/groupguard/query before preparing GroupGuard SnowLuma deployment.

production_rule: The GroupGuard shard implementation and CI are complete, but it must remain undeployed until the compatible lolapisevers delivery endpoint is live. Never restore plugin-side public fallback.
